what: Tools to Help to Publish the Trend-Cycle Component
title: Tools to Help to Publish the Trend-Cycle Component
text: publish trend-cycle? goal publishTC facilitate computation, evaluation, visualization trend-cycle components time series using modern state---art methodology: Using Cascade Linear Filter (CLF) surrogate cut--normalise asymmetric filters, done Statistics Canada (Dagum Luati 2008); Using classical Henderson symmetric filter surrogate Musgrave asymmetric filters, done Australian Bureau Statistics (Trewin 2003); Using local parametrization Musgrave asymmetric filters (Quartier-la-Tente 2024); Extending Henderson filters take account additive outliers (AO) level shifts (LS) (Quartier-la-Tente 2025).

title: Tools to Help to Publish the Trend-Cycle Component
text: Account Additive Outliers (AO) Level Shifts (LS) estimation:
code: # Identify outliers using RegARIMA wrapper outliers <- x13_regarima_outliers(x)  # Compute robust Henderson trend-cycle estimates tc_robust <- henderson_robust_smoothing(   x,    ao = outliers$ao,    ls = outliers$ls,    local_icr = TRUE )  # Segmented smoothing around a structural break tc_seg <- segmented_smoothing(   x,    breaks = list(c(2020, 3)),    break_method = "two-sides" ) plot(tc_robust, xlim = c(2019, 2021)) lines(tc_seg, col_tc = "#009E73") lines(tc_hend, col_tc = "#0072B2") legend(   "bottomleft",   legend = c("Seasonally adjusted (SA)", "Robust Henderson", "Segmented", "Standard Henderson"),   col = c("black", "orange", "#009E73", "#0072B2"),   lty = 1 )

title: Robust Trend-Cycle Estimation using the Henderson Filter — henderson_robust_smoothing
text: outliers present time series, standard linear filters like Henderson moving average can spread impact across adjacent trend estimates. function explicitly accounts specified Additive Outliers (AO) Level Shifts (LS) filtering process prevent distortion trend-cycle estimates described Quartier-la-Tente (2025). nutshell, Henderson smoothing equivalent local polynomial regression degree 3 (equivalently 2) estimated weighted least squares, using specific weights obtain Henderson coefficients. Adding regressors local regression account outliers allows removing influence estimation polynomial coefficients thus trend-cycle estimates.

text: icr() computes overall /C ratio, icrs() computes /C ratios lag series frequency.

title: Compute Irregular-to-Trend-Cycle (I/C) Ratios — icr
code: icr(x, tc, mul = FALSE)  icrs(x, tc, mul = FALSE)

title: Compute Irregular-to-Trend-Cycle (I/C) Ratios — icr
text: x seasonally adjusted time series object class "tc_estimates". tc time series representing trend-cycle component. Ignored x object class "tc_estimates". mul Logical indicating whether decomposition multiplicative (TRUE) additive (FALSE, default).

title: Compute Irregular-to-Trend-Cycle (I/C) Ratios — icr
text: icr() returns single numeric value representing overall /C ratio, icrs() returns named numeric vector /C ratios lags \(1\) \(p\).

title: Compute Irregular-to-Trend-Cycle (I/C) Ratios — icr
text: /C ratio measures relative importance irregular component compared trend-cycle component time series decomposition. time series frequency \(p\), decomposition additive (mul = FALSE), irregular component defined \(I_t = X_t - TC_t\). icrs() returns vector containing ratio mean absolute variation irregular component trend-cycle component lag \(k\): $$ \frac{\bar{}_k}{\bar{C}_k} = \frac{\sum |I_t - I_{t-k}|}{\sum |TC_t - TC_{t-k}|} \quad \text{} k \\{1, 2, \dots, p\}. $$ decomposition multiplicative (mul = TRUE), irregular component defined \(I_t = X_t / TC_t\), ratio relative variations computed : $$ \frac{\bar{}_k}{\bar{C}_k} = \frac{\sum |(I_t - I_{t-k}) / I_{t-k}|}{\sum |(TC_t - TC_{t-k}) / TC_{t-k}|} \quad \text{} k \\{1, 2, \dots, p\}. $$ icr() returns overall /C ratio, corresponds first lag ratio \(\bar{}_1 / \bar{C}_1\).

title: Compute Irregular-to-Trend-Cycle (I/C) Ratios — icr
code: if (FALSE) { # rjd3jars::check_java_version(silent = TRUE) x <- cars_registrations tc <- henderson_smoothing(x) icr(tc) icrs(tc) }

title: Month of Cyclical Dominance (MCD) — mcd
text: Month Cyclical Dominance (MCD) represents minimum number months required average absolute variation trend-cycle component dominate irregular component. words, indicates shortest time span needed average cyclical signal outweigh irregular fluctuations. computed smallest integer \(k\) (\(k \ge 1\)) /C ratio remains less equal 1 lags \(j \ge k\): $$ k = \min \left\{ k \\{1, \dots, p\} : \frac{\bar{}_j}{\bar{C}_j} \le 1 \text{ } j \ge k \right\} $$ /C ratio never falls equal 1 within frequency \(p\), MCD set \(p\).

title: Measure Smoothness of Trend-Cycle Estimates — smoothness
text: Computes smoothness ratio trend-cycle estimates relative seasonally adjusted series following Picard Matthews (2016).

title: Measure Smoothness of Trend-Cycle Estimates — smoothness
text: Smoothness evaluated ratio month--month growth rate variances: $$ 100 \times \sqrt{ \frac{ \sum_t \left( \frac{TC_t - TC_{t-1}}{TC_{t-1}} \right)^2 }{ \sum_t \left( \frac{SA_t - SA_{t-1}}{SA_{t-1}} \right)^2 } } $$ metric quantifies relative variability trend-cycle compared seasonally adjusted series. lower value indicates smoother trend-cycle.

title: Measure Smoothness of Trend-Cycle Estimates — smoothness
text: Picard, F., & Matthews, S. (2016). Addition Trend-Cycle Estimates Selected Publications Statistics Canada. Proceedings Survey Methods Section, Statistical Society Canada (SSC) Annual Meeting. https://ssc.ca/sites/default/files/imce/pdf/picard_ssc2016.pdf

title: Detect Turning Points and Unwanted Ripples in a Time Series — turning_points
text: x input time series (object class "ts"). start, end Numeric vectors specifying start end time interval (e.g., c(2020, 1)) search turning points. digits Integer specifying number decimal digits used comparing values determine turning points. Defaults NULL (rounding). k, m Integers specifying required number preceding (\(k\)) succeeding (\(m\)) observations define local extremum. See details.

title: Detect Turning Points and Unwanted Ripples in a Time Series — turning_points
text: turning_points() returns named list two components: "upturn" "downturn", containing vector dates (empty vectors none found). upturn() downturn() return vector dates corresponding detected upturns downturns, respectively. unwanted_ripples() returns integer representing number unwanted ripples detected series.

title: Detect Turning Points and Unwanted Ripples in a Time Series — turning_points
text: Turning points identified following operational definition adapted Zellner, Hong, Min (1991), typically \(k = 3\) \(m = 1\): upturn occurs time \(t\) : $$y_{t-k} \ge \dots \ge y_{t-1} < y_t \le y_{t+1} \le \dots \le y_{t+m}$$ downturn occurs time \(t\) : $$y_{t-k} \le \dots \le y_{t-1} > y_t \ge y_{t+1} \ge \dots \ge y_{t+m}$$ unwanted ripple defined occurrence two turning points type (two upturns two downturns) occur within 10-month window (.e., short cycles lasting less 11 months).

title: Detect Turning Points and Unwanted Ripples in a Time Series — turning_points
text: Zellner, ., Hong, C., & Min, C. (1991). Forecasting Turning Points International Growth Rates using Bayesian Exponential Smoothing Methods. Journal Econometrics, 49(1–2), 275–304. doi:10.1016/0304-4076(91)90099-H

title: X-11 Selection of Trend-Cycle Filter — x11_trend_selection
text: following procedure used X-11 select length trend filter: Computes /C ratio, \(icr\), Henderson filter length equal series frequency plus 1. selected length depends value \(icr\): \(icr < 1\), selected length 9 monthly data 5 otherwise. \(1 \le icr < 3.5\), selected length \(freq + 1\) (.e., 13 monthly data, 5 quarterly data). \(icr \ge 3.5\), selected length 23 monthly data 7 otherwise. value \(icr\) mapped build Musgrave filters (find_icr()): quarterly data, length 5, \(icr = 0.001\); otherwise, \(icr = 4.5\). frequencies, length less equal 9, \(icr = 1.0\). Else, length less equal 13, \(icr = 3.5\). Else, \(icr = 4.5\).
